project.name: Keerthi ERPNext Web Application
project.purpose: Build a production-oriented, role-aware web application that communicates reliably with the existing ERPNext v16 site and uses real server data.

target_erpnext.deployment_context: Windows 11 + Docker Desktop; Frappe site name frontend
target_erpnext.important_note: Verify the live server and installed custom apps before assuming any custom endpoint exists. Do not store credentials in this JSON.

project.primary_goal: Implement one reusable communication core and generalized ERP engine, then build role-specific modules and dashboards on top of it.

instructions_for_ai_studio.role: Act as a senior full-stack engineer, ERPNext/Frappe v16 integration specialist, security reviewer, and test engineer.
execution_rules: First inspect the complete existing web application project and map its actual framework, routes, UI components, state management, authentication, API calls, tests, and environment variables.
Do not rewrite the project from scratch or replace working components before documenting what exists.
Use supplied Flutter SDK files as behavioral and API-flow references only; do not attempt to import Dart code into a React/Next.js web application.
Inspect the supplied SDK source and tests directly before inferring behavior. Distinguish implemented behavior, test expectations, and assumptions.
Build a file-by-file implementation plan, then implement in small, testable phases.
Preserve existing UI, design tokens, routes, and business functionality unless a change is necessary and documented.
Use actual ERPNext data only. Never silently fall back to mock data or hardcoded dashboard figures.
Do not claim an endpoint works until it has been verified against the target server or clearly label it unverified.
Do not expose API secrets, passwords, session IDs, CSRF tokens, or private keys in browser code, logs, screenshots, or committed files.
Do not bypass ERPNext permission checks or implement accounting ledger posting independently in the browser.
For every meaningful change, provide changed file list, rationale, test commands, test results, and any remaining risks.
instructions_for_ai_studio.first_deliverable: A source-grounded audit report: current architecture, current API paths, actual modules/screens, existing role/permission behavior, test coverage, integration gaps, security issues, and an incremental implementation plan.
avoid: Assuming standard ERPNext roles match the company's custom job roles.
Assuming custom endpoints mobile_sync.* or mobile_auth.* exist on the target server.
Using an unrestricted proxy that accepts arbitrary upstream URLs or arbitrary server method names.
Sending ERPNext API secrets to client-side JavaScript.
Making up business fields, workflow states, reports, or permission assignments.

source_of_truth_order: Current web app code for existing UI and frontend behavior
Live ERPNext server behavior and actual installed apps for endpoint availability and authorization
Flutter SDK implementation for reference behavior
SDK tests for intended or regression-tested behavior
This JSON for requested target architecture and requirements

architecture.pattern: Layered modular monolith with a shared ERP communication core and metadata-driven business engine.

recommended_layers.name: Presentation
responsibilities: Role-aware shell, navigation, dashboard, tables, forms, dialogs, charts, loading states, empty states, and error states.
Use reusable accessible UI components and preserve the existing app design system.

recommended_layers.name: Application/use-case layer
responsibilities: Business use cases such as create sales invoice, receive payment, dispatch delivery, transfer stock, or create employee.
Coordinate validation, API calls, confirmation, refresh, and user feedback.

recommended_layers.name: Domain/module layer
responsibilities: Module registry, DocType configurations, workflow-specific UI rules, report definitions, and typed domain models.
Keep module-specific rules separate from generic HTTP code.

recommended_layers.name: ERP communication core
responsibilities: Authentication/session, request construction, response envelope parsing, error normalization, timeout/cancellation, safe retry policy, request IDs, and structured redacted logging.
Provide typed methods for metadata, list, count, get, create, update, delete, workflow actions, files, and reports.

recommended_layers.name: Secure server adapter
responsibilities: If using Next.js, use server routes/actions for secrets and session-bound operations.
Expose explicit allowlisted operations; never an unrestricted arbitrary URL or method proxy.
Forward authenticated requests to ERPNext and preserve server authorization.

recommended_layers.name: ERPNext/Frappe
responsibilities: Authoritative authentication, permissions, validation, workflow, document lifecycle, stock ledger, accounting ledger, and reports.

recommended_web_stack_if_existing_app_ma.styling: Existing Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui if already installed
recommended_web_stack_if_existing_app_ma.data_fetching: Reuse existing data-fetching library; otherwise choose a consistent query/cache strategy
recommended_web_stack_if_existing_app_ma.charts: Use existing chart library; otherwise use a React chart library such as Recharts
recommended_web_stack_if_existing_app_ma.forms: Schema/metadata-driven reusable form renderer with server errors mapped to fields
recommended_web_stack_if_existing_app_ma.offline: IndexedDB + outbox only if explicitly needed; do not implement Flutter SQLite code in browser

required_services.name: authService
requirements: Use the chosen secure session strategy.
Handle expired sessions predictably.
Never store passwords or long-lived secrets in localStorage.

required_services.name: httpClient
requirements: Same-origin web API calls by default.
JSON and non-JSON response handling.
Timeout and abort support.
Consistent error object including status, safe message, and correlation/request ID when available.
Redact cookies, authorization headers, passwords, tokens, and personal data from logs.

required_services.name: metadataService
requirements: Cache with invalidation and handle permission-denied metadata.
Honor field types, required flags, read-only flags, hidden fields, options, links, and child tables.
Never assume metadata alone grants permission to perform an action.

required_services.name: documentService
requirements: Use explicit typed inputs and outputs.
Validate paging and sort parameters.
Map Frappe server validation messages into visible errors.
Do not retry create/update/delete/submit/cancel blindly.
Confirm destructive and irreversible actions.

required_services.name: permissionService
requirements: Use verified APIs or server-provided permissions.
Treat frontend checks as display logic only.
ERPNext server permission enforcement is authoritative.
Do not hardcode a user as Administrator based on email/name.

required_services.name: workflowService
requirements: Discover workflow/status capabilities from verified metadata or approved endpoints.
Use supported Frappe methods and server-side validation.
Do not fabricate workflow transitions.

required_services.name: reportService
requirements: Use approved report endpoints or custom server methods verified on the target site.
Use date range, company, and permission filters where applicable.
Do not compute official financial statements in the browser from partial document lists.

known_reference_endpoints_from_supplied_.verification: Verify actual response shape and permissions on target site.
Verify supported fields, filters, paging, and permissions.
Standard resource API; test access with least-privilege users.
Test validation, concurrency, and permission failures.
Restrict destructive actions and verify authorization.

known_reference_endpoints_from_supplied_.purpose: Alternative document insert method referenced by SDK
known_reference_endpoints_from_supplied_.verification: Use only if required and verified; do not duplicate create paths without reason.
Custom endpoint; verify app and method exist before use.

known_reference_endpoints_from_supplied_.purpose: Custom bulk document fetch with child tables
known_reference_endpoints_from_supplied_.verification: Custom endpoint; verify app and method exist before use.

known_reference_endpoints_from_supplied_.purpose: Permission service reference from supplied SDK
known_reference_endpoints_from_supplied_.verification: Custom endpoint; verify exact route, app, return shape, and role restrictions.

error_policy.401: Revalidate or clear session and route to login; avoid infinite redirect loops.
error_policy.403: Show permission-denied message; do not retry automatically.
error_policy.404: Show not found or unimplemented endpoint; do not silently return mock data.
error_policy.417_or_422: Show Frappe validation details and field errors when possible.
error_policy.409: Treat as conflict and offer safe refresh/review.
error_policy.429: Respect Retry-After if present; use bounded backoff for safe requests only.
error_policy.5xx: Show a recoverable server error with correlation ID if available.
error_policy.network_or_timeout: Show retry option for safe reads; do not automatically repeat non-idempotent writes.

principles: Read actual ERPNext roles and permissions before finalizing app roles.
The job-role labels below are proposed product personas, not assumed existing ERPNext roles.
Map product personas to one or more actual ERPNext roles through explicit configuration.
Every action must be authorized by ERPNext; the web UI only hides or disables actions for usability.
Use least privilege and test each persona with a real test account.
Never infer role from email, display name, department text, or client-side state.

personas.label: System Administrator
dashboard: System health and API connection status
personas.permission_policy: Use actual Administrator/role permissions from ERPNext; do not automatically grant every custom operation to this persona.

personas.label: Order Biller / Sales Counter
actions: Submit invoices only if actual permissions and workflow allow
Print or export only where authorized
restrictions: No general ledger or journal entry access by default
No unrestricted discounts, price overrides, or write-offs
No payment cancellation/refund unless explicitly authorized

personas.label: Accountant
restrictions: Use server-authorized reports and document actions
Do not independently alter posted ledger rows
Journal creation, posting, reversal, and period closing require explicit server permission

personas.label: Sales Staff
dashboard: Assigned leads or customers if configured
restrictions: Respect territory, owner, company, and document-level restrictions where configured
Do not assume permission to create or submit invoices

personas.label: Stock / Warehouse User
restrictions: Use ERPNext stock transactions and server validation
Do not directly modify stock ledger entries
Company and warehouse scope must be server-authorized

personas.label: Delivery Staff
restrictions: Status transitions must use a verified workflow or approved custom endpoint
Do not invent delivery status fields or workflow states

personas.label: HR User
restrictions: Verify HRMS app and DocTypes exist
Protect employee personal data and salary information
Payroll access must be separately authorized

personas.label: Branch / Operations Manager
restrictions: Show company/branch/team scope only if configured in ERPNext
Approval actions require actual workflow permissions

roles_and_permissions.implementation_requirement: Create a permission adapter that maps real ERPNext roles/permissions to navigation and action visibility. Treat this list as proposed UX policy, not a grant of access.

business_modules.purpose: Role-aware KPI cards and charts using verified real data.
features: Company/branch filters only when supported and authorized
Loading, empty, error, and stale-data states
No hardcoded or mock metrics in production
Quantity, price, discount and tax display from authorized ERP logic
Invoice creation and submission only where authorized
Payment receipt/Payment Entry if configured and authorized
Daily closing report from verified server data
critical_rules: Do not compute authoritative taxes or totals independently in browser.
Do not submit invoices automatically unless explicitly designed and authorized.
Do not silently create a payment merely because an invoice was created.

business_modules.purpose: Financial dashboard, accounting documents, and server-generated reports.
features: Sales Invoice and Purchase Invoice lists
critical_rules: ERPNext is the source of truth for official accounting entries and financial statements.
Never directly edit ledger rows from the web UI.
Verify reports, filters, company, fiscal year, and permissions on the server.
Do not assume every report is available through the generic resource API.
Use ERPNext stock transactions and server validation.
Never edit stock ledger entries directly.
Verify serial/batch and warehouse requirements from metadata and server behavior.

features: Pickup/in-transit/delivered/failed views only if these states exist in configured workflow
Proof of delivery if a supported field/process exists
critical_rules: Inspect actual custom delivery module, fields, and endpoints before implementing.
Do not invent a status field or bypass server workflow.

business_modules.purpose: HR operations using installed HRMS and actual permissions.
features: Payroll only when installed and authorized
critical_rules: Verify HRMS DocTypes and role permissions.

business_modules.purpose: User-facing preferences and authorized integration diagnostics.
features: Version/app status if available from a verified endpoint

global_shell: Current user and company context where available
Notifications only when backed by real sources
Breadcrumbs, keyboard accessibility, and mobile-friendly layout
all_screens_must_have: Retry control only when retry is safe
design_rules: Use the existing design system and components where available.
Avoid building every module as a generic raw table; add workflow-specific UI where needed.
Do not fabricate graphs from sample values in production.
Clearly distinguish Draft, Submitted, Cancelled, and custom statuses using server-returned values.

response_handling: Support Frappe response envelopes such as data and message where applicable.
Preserve structured server validation details for field-level display.
Handle empty bodies and non-JSON responses safely.
Never treat an HTTP 200 response as business success if the returned payload contains a documented application error.
list_queries: Validate fields, filters, order_by, limit_start, and limit_page_length.
Do not expose unrestricted arbitrary method calls to the browser.
write_operations: Use idempotency for create operations only when supported and verified.
Do not blindly retry writes after timeout; first reconcile whether the server committed the operation.
audit_logging: Record safe event type, timestamp, route, status, duration, and correlation ID.
Never log passwords, API secrets, session cookies, authorization headers, full sensitive payloads, or employee financial data.

must: Keep API secrets and server-only credentials outside browser bundles.
Use secure, HttpOnly, appropriately SameSite session cookies if a server session proxy is used.
Implement CSRF defenses appropriate to the session and deployment model.
Validate Origin/Host on state-changing same-origin routes.
Use rate limiting for login and sensitive endpoints.
Use allowlisted server routes and approved upstream paths.
Test unauthorized access using low-privilege test users.
must_not: Expose ERPNext API key/secret in NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables.
Store passwords or session cookies in localStorage.
Trust client-supplied role names or permission booleans.
Use client-side navigation hiding as the only security boundary.
Allow an arbitrary URL proxy or arbitrary Frappe method execution.
Create official accounting/stock ledger records outside ERPNext business APIs.
security.review_note: Any previously generated starter code must be reviewed and tested before production; in particular, verify cookie parsing, CSRF behavior, session validation, proxy restrictions, and error propagation.

offline_and_sync.default: Do not implement offline sync until requirements and conflict semantics are agreed.
if_required: Use IndexedDB for web local persistence, not Flutter sqflite APIs.
Create an explicit outbox with operation IDs and status.
Define which DocTypes can be cached and which fields are sensitive.
Protect local dirty records from overwrite.
Define three-way conflict handling per document type.
Use idempotency or server reconciliation before retrying create operations.
Show pending, synced, failed, and conflict states.
Never queue irreversible financial or stock posting operations for silent background submission without a deliberate, audited workflow.

phase_1_static_review: Map every existing API call and endpoint.
Identify mock/stub data and remove only after replacing with verified live integration.
Identify secrets and unsafe browser-side requests.
Inspect dependencies, routes, components, and test setup.
phase_3_integration_tests: List and fetch a permitted document
Create/update a harmless test document if authorized
Verify permission-denied behavior with restricted user
Verify invalid input returns a visible validation error
Verify missing custom endpoint fails visibly without mock fallback
phase_4_business_tests: Biller can only perform assigned billing actions
Accountant can access only permitted accounting documents/reports
Stock user cannot access unauthorized accounting or HR records
Delivery user only sees authorized/assigned delivery records
No double submit on repeated clicks or network interruption
phase_5_release: Run type checking, lint, unit tests, and production build.
Test on staging or with low-privilege accounts before production.
Document environment setup, rollback, and known limitations.

implementation_phases.name: Audit existing web app
exit_criteria: Mock data and integration gaps listed

implementation_phases.name: Communication and session core
exit_criteria: Integration tests pass against test account

implementation_phases.name: Metadata and permission engine
exit_criteria: Role/permission adapter based on actual server data
Generic list and document detail APIs

implementation_phases.name: Role-aware business UI
exit_criteria: Actual roles mapped to proposed personas
Biller, accounts, stock, delivery, HR screens scoped to permissions

implementation_phases.name: Accounts and operational workflows
exit_criteria: Stock workflows use standard business APIs

implementation_phases.name: Hardening and optional offline support
exit_criteria: Offline sync implemented only if required

completion_definition: The app uses verified live ERPNext APIs for all claimed real-data features.
There is one shared communication core rather than duplicated per-module networking.
All role assignments derive from actual server roles/permissions and explicit mapping.
Accounts and stock data come from authoritative ERPNext services/reports.
No production path silently falls back to mocks.
Authentication, permission failures, validation, network failures, and duplicate-submit risks are tested.
Type check, lint, tests, and production build pass, with results reported truthfully.
